gloss: stocking up; keeping a supply on hand

definitions.gloss: stocking up in advance; a stock kept on hand
definitions.explanation: Buying everyday items before they are needed so that a supply is always available, or the supply itself. Used of household staples such as rice, detergent, and toilet paper.

examples.japanese: {洗剤|せんざい}の{買|か}い{置|お}きがある。
{買|か}い{置|お}きしておいてよかった。
examples.english: I'm glad I stocked up beforehand.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{置|お}きが{切|き}れたので、{帰|かえ}りにスーパーに{寄|よ}ってきます。
examples.english: We're out of our stock, so I'll stop by the supermarket on the way home.

notes:
Composed of {買|か}う (to buy) + {置|お}く (to leave in place). Takes する to form a verb: {買|か}い{置|お}きする.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {買|か}い{置|お}きしておく: to buy some to keep on hand
- {買|か}い{置|お}きがある: to have a stock of something
- {買|か}い{置|お}きが{切|き}れる: to run out of one's stock

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {買|か}いだめ: hoarding — larger quantities, often driven by anxiety about shortages
- {買|か}い{足|た}す: to buy more — restocking after running short, the opposite timing
- {備蓄|びちく}: stockpile — formal, about emergency or national reserves
